en: The *Sūtra on Maitreya’s Coming*,
translated anonymously and appended to the Eastern Jin records,
states that Śāriputra was the foremost disciple of the Buddha; with a heart of compassion, he took all under heaven into his thoughts and went forth.
Arriving before the Buddha, he knelt with his hands joined in reverence and asked:
"The Buddha has often said:
'After the Buddha’s passing, Maitreya shall come.'"
"I wish to hear this from the Buddha.
The Buddha said,
"When Maitreya Buddha is about to appear in the world, all the mountains, trees, grasses, and woods within Jambudvīpa will be completely scorched away."

At present, the land of Jambudvīpa is sixty thousand li in circumference; when Maitreya appears, Jambudvīpa will be four hundred thousand li long from east to west and three hundred and twenty thousand li wide from south to north. The ground shall produce five kinds of fruits and melons, and within the four seas there will be no mountains, hills, ravines, or valleys; the earth will be as level as a whetstone, and all trees will grow tall and large.

"At that time, there will be few among the people who are greedy, lustful, angry, or ignorant; the population will be vast, with people living in villages and households where the crowing of roosters can be heard echoing from one to another. All the people will have a lifespan of eighty-four thousand years, women will not marry until they are five hundred years old, and the people will be free from illness and pain."
All people in the world have three ailments:
first, the desire to obtain something;
second, hunger and thirst.
Third, as for his advanced age:
the faces of the people were all the color of peach blossoms, and the people all held him in deep respect.

There was a city named Kikuta; this city of Kikuta was the capital where the kingdom was governed. The city was four hundred and eighty *li* in circumference. It was built with earth, further reinforced with wooden planks, and then adorned with gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, and various precious gems.
Each of the four sides has twelve gates, all of which are intricately carved and adorned with gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, and various precious gems.
The king’s name is Saṃghara; all within the four seas belong to Saṃghara. When he travels, he flies through the air, and wherever he goes, the people and spirits alike bow down in reverence.
"The city possesses four treasures:
first, gold, which is guarded by a dragon named Niṣka; this dragon presides over the protection of the gold, and the mountain where the dragon dwells is named Gandha.
Second, silver; within that kingdom there is another guardian dragon named Patadhū."
Third is the moon-bright pearl; the place where it is produced is named Sūjāta, and the treasure-guarding dragon there is named Piṅgala.
Fourth is lapis lazuli; the city where it is produced is named Vaṃśanagara.
“There shall be a brahmin named Sūvan who will be the father of Maitreya.
Maitreya’s mother shall be named Mahāprajāpatī, and Maitreya shall be her son.”
Maitreya shall be born into the caste of Brahmins; his body will possess the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics, and he will be sixteen zhang tall.
Maitreya will be born in the city of Tuṣita; his vision will penetrate for ten thousand li within, and the light from a sun upon his head will illuminate four thousand li.
When Maitreya attains the Way and becomes a Buddha, he will sit beneath a Dragon-flower tree; the tree is forty *li* high and forty *li* wide.
When Maitreya attains Buddhahood, there will be eighty-four thousand Brahmins who all go to where Maitreya is to serve him as their teacher, and they shall renounce their homes to become śramaṇas.
Maitreya sat beneath a tree and attained the Way of the Buddha on the eighth day of the fourth month at the time of the rising of the morning star.

When King Saṃvara heard that Maitreya had attained Buddhahood, he took eighty-four kings and together they all abandoned their kingdoms and renounced their royal status, entrusting the nations to their crown princes; they went together to the place where Maitreya Buddha was and shaved off their hair and beards to become śramaṇas.
Furthermore, there were one thousand eight hundred brahmins who all went to where Maitreya Buddha was and became śramaṇas; Maitreya’s parents were also among them.
Additionally, there were one thousand eighty-four noble brahmins who likewise went to where Maitreya Buddha was and became śramaṇas.
"In this kingdom there was a great and eminent man named Sudatta, whom people also called Sudāsa; he gave gold to Maitreya Buddha and the various śramaṇas, and his fame spread daily far and wide."
Sudatta again led fourteen thousand virtuous people to the place where Maitreya Buddha was, and they became śramaṇas.
Furthermore, there were two brothers; the elder was named Guda and the younger was named Pula. The brothers both said:
"Why do we remain in this world?"
"Would it not be better for us both to go to the Buddha's presence and seek ordination as śramaṇas?
Both brothers said, "If it is well,
let us go together to Maitreya Buddha’s place and become śramaṇas."

"Furthermore, there were eighty-four thousand young women, all wearing fine garments and adorned with white pearls, gold, silver, and necklaces. They went together to where Maitreya Buddha was, removed the precious jewels from their bodies and placed them on the ground, and said to the Buddha:
'We wish to offer these to the Buddha and the various śramaṇas; we wish to become bhikṣuṇīs under the Buddha.'"
The Buddha then immediately ordained her as a bhikṣuṇī.

When Maitreya Buddha sat upon his throne, he preached to the assembly of bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, saying: "All of you were, during the time of Śākyamuni Buddha, those who recited the sūtras, those with compassionate hearts, those who practiced giving, those who were free from anger, those who built monasteries and temples, those who enshrined the Buddha’s relics within stūpas, those who burned incense, those who lit lamps, those who hung silk banners, those who scattered flowers, and those who read the scriptures."

These bhikṣuṇīs were all contemporaries of Śākyamuni Buddha; they were those who upheld the precepts and were possessed of utmost sincerity. They have now all come to this assembly, and those among them who heard the sūtras preached by the bhikṣus shall all attain the Way beneath the Dragon Flower tree.
"When Maitreya Buddha preaches the sutras during his first assembly, nine hundred and sixty million people will all attain the path of Arhatship.
During his second assembly when he preaches the sutras, nine hundred and forty million bhikṣus will all attain Arhatship."
"At the third assembly where the sutra is preached, ninety-two billion śramaṇas will all attain arhatship.
All the devas throughout the heavens shall take up flowers and scatter them over the body of Maitreya."

“Maitreya Buddha shall lead all the Arhats to the city governed by King Kikī; the king will provide them with meals within his inner palace, and the entire city will be as bright as if it were daytime, even during the night.”
Maitreya sat within the palace and preached a sutra, saying:
"Speech must not be left unpracticed; the Way must not be left unstudied; the sutras must not be left unpraised."

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, all the bhikṣus, the king, and his hundred officials shall all practice the precepts of the Buddha’s sutras and all attain deliverance from the world.
Thus spoke the Buddha: "Sixty *koṭis* and sixty thousand years remaining thereafter, Maitreya Buddha shall descend."
The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on Maitreya’s Coming to Rebirth in This World.
